description.value: The study examined whole-brain BOLD responses to beverage-related visual cues in patients with alcohol use disorder and healthy controls.

spans.text: Here, we examined whole-brain blood oxygen level-dependent (BOLD) responses to behavioural cues in individuals with AUD and in healthy controls (HCs).

value: In AUD patients, we hypothesized that the presentation of stimuli involving alcohol-drinking behaviour may be accompanied by stronger brain activation than stimuli that simply contain alcoholic beverages.
We anticipated that such alterations might be correlated with changes in cognitive function in the patient group.

We performed fMRI statistical analysis on the preprocessed EPIs with the general linear model (GLM) using a two-level approach [ 18 ].
Image processing and statistical analyses were performed using the statistical parametric mapping software SPM12 [ 17 ] with MATLAB R2015a.
The first five volumes of each EPI image run were excluded to allow the MR signal to reach a state of equilibrium.
The normalized functional images were smoothed with a 3D 8-mm full width at half-maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel.

description.value: DICOM functional images were converted to NIFTI using MRI-Convert, then processed in SPM12: the first five EPI volumes were discarded, images were realigned, slice-time corrected, coregistered to each participant's T1 image, normalized to ICBM 152 MNI space, spatially smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel, and temporally high-pass filtered at 128 seconds. Six motion parameters were retained for later modeling.
